decisions.reason: Uses host-input-contract.ts and host-input-facade.ts to distinguish clipboard-text projection values (InputState.draft, Occurrence.offset/length, EditorProjection.clipboardText, chips expanded to clipboardText) from detect-coordinate spans (detectText, TokenSpan, one U+FFFC per chip) spliced by insertReference/consumeToken, with plain text and separator spaces keeping normal width in both.

Locates snapshot.draft.length in plugin-client.js add and connects the log numbers (draft length 29 vs detectText length 2 after the first chip) to the failed detect-span splice returning false, which the plugin turns into its changed-composer toast; explains the empty-composer coincidence for paste #1 and the growing overshoot for later pastes, and explicitly rules out a real concurrent edit (rev CAS passes).

Traces plugin-client.js remove: occurrence.offset/length passed unconverted (end = 0+28) to consumeToken against a 2-char detect text, the false return ignored, records.delete and changed() run anyway — leaving the live occurrence rendered with a missing record so the dock shows 'unavailable' and the composer chip persists; both symptoms tied to the single coordinate mismatch, not a separate upload failure.

Derives toDetect(c) = c minus the sum of (occurrence.length - 1) over fully preceding occurrences from the sealed contract, applies it at both call sites (insert at draft end accounting for all preceding chips, removal mapping occurrence.offset to a one-detect-character span), keeps the draftRev guard by computing from the same snapshot, and retires records only when consumeToken (or the setDraft fallback) actually applied, surfacing an error otherwise.

Proposes two successive pastes asserting both chips/occurrences present (plus Nth-paste and mixed-text variants), removal of a chip with another chip present (first-chip, middle-of-three, last-chip variants) asserting composer occurrence, dock chip and record removed together while the other chip survives, and a declined-consumption test asserting the record is kept and no 'unavailable' ghost appears.
